newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Asia satellite operator ACeS signs $545 mln deals.
newsitem.headline: Asia satellite operator ACeS signs $545 mln deals.

text.p: Satellite operator PT Asia Cellular Satellite (ACeS), owned by three Southeast Asian countries, said it signed deals worth around $545 million on Tuesday to further its cellular telephone project.

The deals included a $70 million contract with Lockheed Martin Khrunichev Enterprises for the launch of ACeS's Garuda satellite, president director Adi Adiwoso told reporters after a signing ceremony.
Lockheed Martin Khrunichev Enterprises is a consortium of Lockheed Martin Corporation of the United States and Russian aerospace firms.
ACeS also signed a deal worth $225 million with Swedish telecommunications giant Ericcson for a handset procurement contract, Adiwoso said.
The satellite operator at the same time also signed a financing underwriting agreement with state-owned PT Danareksa Finance worth $250 million, he said.

ACeS is equally owned by Indonesia's PT Pasifik Satelit Nusantara, the Philipine Long Distance Telephone Company and Thailand's Jasmine International Overseas Company, Ltd which is a subdiary of Jasmine International Public Company Ltd.

Adiwoso said the firm offered the contract to the Lockheed consortium following its high percentage of successful launches compared to other satellite launchers in western Europe and in the United States.
"Compared to other launchers, the Russian partnership offers cost which is very competitive, that is around half of others, and higher success rate," Adiwoso said.
The ACeS's Garuda satellite has been under construction for the past fourteen months at Lockheed Martin's facilities in the United States.

The satellite will be placed in orbit during a launch window scheduled between July to September 1998 on a Proton rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in the Republic of Kazakhstan, said Paul Mellon, Lockheed Martin programme director for ACeS.
The ACeS system is expected to be commercial from January 1999, Adiwoso said.
Adiwoso said the more than $225 million deal with Ericsson invloved an initial order to manufacture the dual-mode satellite-cellular handsets.
The handsets will be capable of communicating directly with the Garuda satellite as well as connecting with local terrestrial cellular and fixed telephone networks.
Adiwoso said the $250 million underwriting agreement with Danareksa, the international tranche of which is to be arranged by ING Bank, represented the final tranche of funding.
ACeS, with an estimated cost of around $700 million, had earlier secured some $210 million loan from shareholders. Its total paid-up capital is $210 million.
